jobs.title: Strategic Account Executive - Singapore
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Singapore
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role
As a Strategic Account Executive for Singapore, you will own and grow GitLab’s enterprise relationships in the Singapore market. You’ll help large organizations realize the full value of GitLab’s AI-powered DevSecOps platform by leading the entire sales cycle, from prospecting and qualification through rollout and long-term adoption. Reporting to an Area Sales Manager or Regional Director, you’ll use a consultative approach to understand complex customer needs, guide them through evaluation, and coordinate pre- and post-sales resources to ensure successful deployments and visible business outcomes.
You’ll work under minimal supervision on complex deals, act as the voice of the customer into GitLab, and partner closely with our strategic channel partners to generate qualified opportunities and develop new customers. In your first year, you’ll be expected to establish and execute clear account plans for enterprise prospects and customers in the Singapore market, build strong internal and external stakeholder relationships, and consistently manage your forecast and pipeline with transparency and discipline.

What you’ll do

• Support GitLab’s strategic prospects and customers in the Singapore Market, owning the full sales cycle for large and enterprise accounts

• Lead account strategy by developing and executing account plans aligned to each customer’s business needs and long-term goals

• Conduct prospecting and opportunity development activities in named large and strategic accounts, including working closely with strategic channel partners to generate qualified leads and new customers

• Coordinate pre- and post-sales engagement with solutions architects, customer success, and support teams to ensure successful rollout, adoption, and expansion of GitLab products

• Provide clear account leadership, including regular activity, pipeline, and forecast reporting to sales management

• Analyze wins and losses, contribute to root cause analysis, and share lessons learned with account managers, marketing, and technical teams to improve future outcomes

• Act as the voice of the customer by sharing feedback and product ideas through GitLab’s public issue tracker and internal channels

• Use a consultative sales approach to uncover business issues, shape solution recommendations, and deliver compelling proposals, quotes, and presentations that address customer requirements

What you’ll bring

• Experience managing complex sales cycles with large, strategic enterprise customers.

• Proven ability to prospect, qualify, and develop new opportunities while also growing existing accounts through strong account management

• Skill in leading pre- and post-sales activities, coordinating with technical, support, and channel partners to drive adoption and expansion

• Proficiency in consultative selling, including uncovering business needs, building account plans, and delivering proposals and presentations that align GitLab solutions to customer outcomes

• Ability to prepare and maintain accurate activity, pipeline, and forecast reports, and to contribute to win/loss and root cause analysis

• Effective communication and collaboration skills to share customer feedback and lessons learned with sales management, product, marketing, and technical teams

• Familiarity with software development concepts and tools, with preferred exposure to Git, software development tools, or application lifecycle management

• Alignment with GitLab’s values, openness to learning, and interest in applying transferable skills even if your background does not match every requirement exactly

About the team
The Strategic Account Executive will join our enterprise sales team, which focuses on driving GitLab adoption with large customers in the Singapore market. The team is responsible for the full relationship lifecycle with enterprise accounts, from initial engagement through long-term expansion and advocacy, ensuring customers realize value from GitLab’s DevSecOps platform. Team members work in an all-remote, distributed environment and collaborate asynchronously across time zones with sales leadership, solutions architects, customer success, marketing, and channel partners. The team is currently focused on maintaining and growing our existing footprint in the region, executing a consistent global sales motion while adapting to local customer needs and partnering closely with strategic channel organizations to reach and support key accounts.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

• Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being

• Flexible Paid Time Off

• Team Member Resource Groups

• Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Growth and Development Fund

• Parental Leave

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.
Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.
Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.
GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law . If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation , please let us know during the recruiting process .

jobs.description:
What is Equisoft ? Equisoft is a global provider of digital solutions for insurance and investments, recognized by more than 300 of the world’s leading financial institutions. We offer a comprehensive ecosystem of scalable solutions that help our customers navigate the challenges of digital transformation – powered by a business needs-driven approach, deep industry knowledge, cutting-edge technologies, and multicultural team of experts based in North America, the Caribbean, Latin America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia.

Why Choose Equisoft ? With 850+ employees, we are a stable organization that offers career advancement opportunities and fosters a stimulant environment. If that’s not enough, then check out these other perks below:

• Hiring Location: India

• You are going to work fully remote

• Internal job title: Workday Adaptive Planning Specialist

• Full-time Permanent Role

• Benefits available day 1: Medical, Dental, Term Life/Personal Accident Coverage, Wellness Sessions, telemedicine program, etc.

• Flexible hours

• Number of hours per week: 40

• Educational Support (LinkedIn Learning, LOMA Courses and Equisoft University)

Role: The Workday Adaptive Planning Support/Configuration reports to the Director, FP&A and works closely with a team of 3 FP&A. The incumbent will be responsible for the design, build, and ongoing optimization of Workday Adaptive Planning models, reports, dashboards, and integrations that support the company’s financial planning and reporting needs. Also, serves as the primary technical owner of the Adaptive Planning environment, partnering with Finance leadership, Accounting, Revenue Operations, and IT to deliver scalable and accurate planning solutions.

Your Day with Equisoft :

• Design and maintain sheet structures, account hierarchies, dimension frameworks, and version strategies across budget, forecast, actuals, and scenario versions.

• Ensure calculated accounts, time rollups, and level rollups are configured correctly so that metrics aggregate as intended.

• Diagnose and resolve data load errors, formula conflicts, and configuration issues on a timely basis to minimize disruption to planning and reporting cycles.

• Own the ticket lifecycle with the Adaptive Planning vendor support team, escalating technical issues, tracking resolution timelines, and ensuring follow-through.

• Build recurring reports in Adaptive Planning, Office Connect, and NetSuite to support monthly close, board reporting, and operational decision-making.

• Create interactive dashboards with appropriate filters, drill-through capabilities, and visualizations that communicate performance clearly to stakeholders.

• Define and configure key performance metrics within the model (e.g., ARR, bookings attainment, gross margin, OpEx ratios) with sound calculation methodologies.

• Leverage multi-disciplinary data and work with key stakeholders to develop and enhance a bottom-up, resource-driven capacity model (revenue and cost).

• Own inbound integrations from NetSuite, HRIS, CRM, and other source systems into Adaptive, and design outbound feeds as needed.

• Implement reconciliation checks between source systems and Adaptive, establish validation rules, and maintain audit trails for data loads.

• Build and maintain saved searches and financial reports in NetSuite to complement the Adaptive environment.

• Develop documentation and provide hands-on support to FP&A analysts and budget owners on data entry, report generation, and system functionality.

• Define naming conventions, change management procedures, and access control policies for the Adaptive environment.

• Identify opportunities to extend Adaptive capabilities and partner with stakeholders to prioritize enhancements.

Requirements:

Technical

• Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering or Information Technology or College Diploma combined to 3 years of relevant experience

• 5–7 years of hands-on experience building and administering models in Workday Adaptive Planning (formerly Adaptive Insights).

• Experience with NetSuite reporting and integrating NetSuite data into Adaptive.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills including complex modeling, pivot tables, lookups, and charting.

• Strong understanding of FP&A processes: budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and management reporting.

• Familiarity with financial statement structures and how they translate into planning model design.

• Experience working with European or North American compagnies

• Detail-oriented with a commitment to accuracy in financial reporting.

• Effective communicator who can translate between finance stakeholders and technical platform capabilities.

• Excellent knowledge of English (spoken and written)

Soft skills

• Strong sense of organization and prioritizing

• Analytical and problem-solving skills

• Ability to communicate, write and synthesize information

• Ability to multi-task in a rapid-paced environment

• Team spirit, tact, diplomacy, autonomy, rigor, and discipline

Nice to Haves:

• Experience with SaaS financial metrics such as ARR/MRR, net revenue retention, and booking analysis.

• Experience with workforce planning in Workday: headcount modeling, compensation components, and fully loaded cost calculations.

• Experience with the integration of Workday Adaptive Planning within any form of CRM

• Exposure to business intelligence or data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker).

• Familiarity with additional source system integrations (Workday HCM, ADP, or similar).

Equisoft is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.title: PLM Analyst
jobs.description:
About Us
With electric vehicles expected to be nearly 30% of new vehicle sales by 2025 and more than 50% by 2040, electric mobility is becoming a reality. ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT) is at the center of this revolution, powering one of the world’s leading EV charging networks and a comprehensive set of hardware, software and mobile solutions for every charging need across North America and Europe. We bring together drivers, businesses, automakers, policymakers, utilities and other stakeholders to make e-mobility a global reality.
Since our founding in 2007, ChargePoint has focused solely on making the transition to electric easy for businesses, fleets and drivers. ChargePoint offers a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create an all-electric future and a trillion-dollar market.
At ChargePoint , we foster a positive and productive work environment by committing to live our values of Be Courageous, Charge Together, Love our Customers, Operate with Openness, and Relentlessly Pursue Awesome. These values guide how we show up every day, align, and work together to build a brighter future for all of us.
Join the team that is building the EV charging industry and make your mark on how people and goods will get everywhere they need to go, in any context, for generations to come.

PLM analyst

Reports To

Senior Manager, PLM/MCAD

Role Summary
As a PLM analyst at ChargePoint , you will play a critical role in advancing our mission to transition the world to electric mobility. By ensuring the accuracy, quality, and integrity of our product lifecycle data, you will empower our engineering and operations teams to build and scale world-class EV charging solutions. This role is essential for maintaining the vital technical documentation and configurations that bring our innovative hardware to market reliably and efficiently.

What You Will Be Doing
In this role, you will take ownership of document control and product lifecycle management processes utilizing Arena PLM. You will act as the central hub for product structures, bill of materials (BOM), and change management, ensuring seamless collaboration across engineering, program management, and operations. Day-to-day, you will process engineering change orders, manage part numbers, and enforce strict revision controls. Success in your first 6 to 12 months means establishing yourself as a trusted cross-functional partner who reliably tracks and expedites product changes to keep critical hardware programs on schedule.

What You Will Bring to ChargePoint

• Create and maintain accurate product Bill of Materials (BOM) configurations and complex product structures.

• Drive the creation, processing, and implementation of Engineering Change Orders (ECO) to keep hardware projects on track.

• Generate and manage part numbers in strict adherence to ChargePoint 's numbering schemes and release processes.

• Partner with mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, program management, and operations to align deliverables with dynamic program schedules.

• Develop and maintain strong cross-functional relationships to effectively track changes, resolve bottlenecks, and expedite product deliveries.

• Receive, process, manage, control, and archive company and customer documents, guaranteeing absolute accuracy and data integrity.

• Ensure all assigned deliverables are completed on time to support fast-paced program and manufacturing schedules.

• Enforce compliance with revision control, change management, and supplier collaboration standards across all product lines.

• Identify opportunities to optimize PLM processes and tools, continually improving our configuration management practices.

Requirements

• 1 to 2 years of professional experience in PLM, Document Control, Change Management, or Configuration Management.

• Strong hands-on knowledge of Arena PLM software or equivalent enterprise product lifecycle management tools.

• Deep understanding of product lifecycle management fundamentals, including product structures, multi-level assemblies, and release processes.

• Proven ability to navigate complex engineering environments, managing revision control and supplier collaboration effectively.

• Excellent communication skills with a track record of charging together alongside technical, operational, and program management teams.

Location

India-Remote

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Model Risk Management (R14365)
jobs.description:
Who We Are
Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

Location Note
We’re excited to consider talent currently based in India, as well as candidates who are open to relocating to India for this opportunity. Please note that, as this is a "Remote–India" position, the role must be performed from within India.

The Opportunity
We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join Oportun ’s Model Risk Management team and help provide independent oversight of models used across the business. You’ll evaluate model design, methodology, assumptions, implementation, performance, and ongoing monitoring to help ensure models are appropriate, well-controlled, and aligned with Oportun ’s risk-management standards.
This is a senior individual contributor role that combines quantitative analysis, independent model validation, governance, and cross-functional influence. You’ll work closely with model developers, Risk, Data Science, Compliance, Internal Audit, and other stakeholders to challenge model approaches, identify material risks, and strengthen model risk practices across Oportun .
At Oportun , we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in.

What You'll Do

Your day-to-day

• You’ll independently review and validate statistical, machine learning, and decisioning models used across Oportun , including models supporting consumer credit loss forecasting, liquidity and funding, and capital markets activities.

• You’ll assess model methodology, assumptions, data quality, feature selection, implementation, performance, stability, and limitations.

• You’ll perform quantitative testing, benchmarking, sensitivity analysis, back-testing, and other validation activities.

• You’ll review model monitoring frameworks and help identify performance deterioration, emerging risks, and areas requiring remediation.

• You’ll evaluate model documentation for completeness, clarity, reproducibility, and alignment with model risk management standards.

• You’ll provide effective challenges to model developers and business stakeholders while maintaining constructive working relationships.

• You’ll communicate validation findings, model risks, limitations, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

• You’ll support model governance processes, including model inventory, risk tiering, validation scheduling, issue tracking, and remediation follow-up.

• You’ll partner with Risk, Compliance, Data Science, Product, Engineering, and other teams to strengthen model controls and governance practices.

• You’ll help improve model risk frameworks, validation methodologies, documentation standards, monitoring practices, and governance processes.

• You’ll use data and analytics to identify trends and emerging risks across the model portfolio.

• You’ll look for thoughtful ways to use AI tools to improve research, analysis, documentation, testing, and model risk workflows while maintaining appropriate human review.

• You'll look for ways to use AI tools thoughtfully — to work smarter, reduce manual work, and make better decisions faster

Who You Are

The right fit looks like this
You’re a rigorous and curious quantitative professional who enjoys understanding how models work, where they can fail, and how their risks should be managed. You’re comfortable challenging assumptions, asking detailed questions, and supporting your conclusions with clear analysis.
You combine technical depth with strong judgment and communication skills. You can work independently, explain complex quantitative issues clearly, and build credibility with model developers and senior stakeholders.
You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and expect the same in return.

What You Bring

Skills & experience

Required

• 5+ years of experience in data science, model validation, model risk management, quantitative risk, statistics, or a related field.

• Strong understanding of statistical modeling and machine learning techniques such as logistic regression, gradient boosting, decision trees, neural networks, or similar methods.

• Strong understanding of how defaults, recoveries, prepayments, loan seasoning, and macroeconomic conditions influence consumer loan portfolio losses and cash flows.

• Experience developing or validating consumer credit loss forecasting models using methods such as vintage/cohort analysis, roll-rate or transition models, survival analysis, time-series models, or probability of default (PD), loss given default (LGD), and exposure at default (EAD) frameworks.Strong proficiency in Python, R, SQL, or similar quantitative programming tools.

• Experience working with large datasets and performing advanced statistical analysis, model testing, or performance evaluation.

• Strong understanding of model validation techniques, performance metrics, benchmarking, sensitivity analysis, stability analysis, and ongoing monitoring.

• Experience evaluating model assumptions, data quality, limitations, implementation, and business use.

• Experience independently leading complex analytical or validation work from scoping through final conclusions.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical findings and explain complex model risks clearly.

• Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work independently while partnering effectively with model developers, Risk, Compliance, and senior stakeholders.

Nice to Have

• Experience in model risk management or independent model validation.

• Experience with credit risk, fraud risk, consumer lending, fintech, banking, or another regulated financial services environment.

• Familiarity with model governance frameworks, model inventories, risk tiering, validation schedules, issue management, or regulatory expectations.

• Experience validating machine learning or AI models.

• Experience developing or validating liquidity, funding, or cash-flow forecasting models, including evaluating funding needs and liquidity under stress scenarios.

• Familiarity with capital markets models used for loan valuation or securitization, including assessing how key assumptions affect valuations and projected cash flows.Experience with AWS, SageMaker, Databricks, or other cloud-based analytics and modeling platforms.

• Experience with Spark, PySpark, Hive, or other large-scale data technologies.

• Master’s degree or PhD in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Economics, Finance, or another quantitative discipline.

• Experience using AI-assisted tools to support research, coding, documentation, validation, or quantitative analysis.

Our AI Mindset

We build with AI. We lead with judgment.
AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work.
We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle.
In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together .

Why Oportun

What's in it for you
Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment.

Would you love building agentic systems and ML models to help Sales and Marketing teams decide on what to do next?

Join our Decision Intelligence team
Our Decision Intelligence team develops advanced AI solutions to support Akamai's Sales and Marketing organizations. We collaborate as a dedicated product team, transforming ambiguous commercial challenges into robust, production-grade machine .

Partner with the best
As a Senior Data Scientist, you will independently lead initiatives from problem framing to production, combining enterprise data and external intent signals to deliver actionable insights and measurable business impact to leadership.
As a Senior Data Scientist, you will be responsible for:

• Prioritizing commercial challenges from Sales Operations and Decision Intelligence into well-scoped data science and agentic AI solutions, to validated directly.

• Defining clear project scope, hypotheses, success criteria, exit criteria, and dependencies before development to ensure alignment with business objectives.

• Doing rapidly undefined prototype and iterate on solutions to evaluate feasibility and business impact before advancing successful models into production.

About the Role
We are seeking a Manager, Accounts Payable to lead Accounts Payable and Expense operations. This role will manage individual contributors and may oversee team leads while ensuring invoices, payments, reconciliations, tax reporting, and employee expenses are processed accurately and on time.
The Manager, Accounts Payable will own team performance and execution while driving process improvements, automation, and reporting. You will work across Procurement, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance, and other teams to resolve complex issues, strengthen controls, and improve the procure-to-pay experience.
The ideal candidate is a reliable people leader who uses business context and data to make decisions, advises stakeholders, and delivers measurable operational improvements.

What You’ll Do

• Lead, coach, and develop AP and Expense team members.

• Manage team performance, staffing, workload allocation, and day-to-day execution.

• Build a high-performing team with clear expectations, strong accountability, and consistent results.

• Oversee invoice processing, purchase order matching, coding, approvals, payments, vendor inquiries, and employee expense operations.

• Ensure AP and Expense activities are completed accurately, on time, and in accordance with company policies and controls.

• Own balance sheet reconciliations, AP close activities, accrual support, aging reviews, and related reporting.

• Lead annual 1099 reporting and support other AP-related tax and compliance requirements.

• Serve as the primary AP contact for internal and external audits, ensuring requested documentation is accurate and complete.

• Monitor unmatched invoices, open purchase orders, payment exceptions, duplicate payments, credits, and other outstanding items.

• Identify inefficiencies across AP and Expenses and lead process improvements that increase accuracy, efficiency, and scalability;

• Drive automation and AI initiatives related to invoice processing, matching, approvals, reconciliations, exception handling, and reporting.

• Develop reporting and insights using tools such as Zip, Ramp, Tableau, ERP systems, and other operational data sources.

• Establish and monitor performance metrics, including processing volume, aging, cycle times, exception rates, and on-time payments.

• Partner across Procurement, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance, and business teams and lead cross-functional initiatives when needed.

• Evaluate complex issues using business context, advise team members and stakeholders, and recommend practical solutions.

• Escalate risks and issues that could affect costs, controls, service levels, or short-term business goals.

What You’ll Bring

• 7+ years of experience in accounts payable, Expenses, accounting operations, or procure-to-pay, including people-management experience.

• Proven ability to lead teams, manage performance, and deliver reliable results.

• Experience owning and improving an operational area with measurable impact.

You'll own defined risk analysis projects from investigation through recommendation, working closely with the DCO risk lead and partnering with Product, Operations, and Finance to turn analysis into practical risk decisions that shape a growing business.
What you'll do:

• Analyze clearing-member positions, collateral, settlement obligations, and concentrations, investigating meaningful changes and exceptions and recommending follow-up actions.

• Partner with Product, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Compliance to evaluate how funding, settlement, and processing failures create financial risk across the trade lifecycle, and help draft and maintain related risk procedures and control documentation.

• Prepare concise risk analyses, incident reviews, and management materials that clearly separate confirmed facts, assumptions, open questions, and recommendations.

• Working knowledge of derivatives products and margin models, including how trades create positions, funding needs, and settlement obligations, and how initial and variation margin protect against counterparty exposure.

• Familiarity with clearing risk concepts such as stress and backtesting, collateral management, or settlement exception analysis.

• Demonstrated ability to take an open-ended risk question, structure a work plan, source the right data, and deliver a considered recommendation with minimal direction.

• Sound judgment on escalation: You know when an issue requires deeper investigation versus immediate action, and you communicate your limitations clearly.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

About the Job:
Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.
As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”
Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.
This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

• Product & Value
• Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.

• Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

• Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.

• Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.

• Change & Adoption
• Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.

• Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.

• Executive & Growth
• Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.

• Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.

• Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)
• Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.

• Delivery & Execution
• Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.

• Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.

• Customer Landscape
• Our customers struggle with long lead times, risky deployments, feature flag sprawl, unclear ownership of releases, and a gap between what engineering ships and what the business expects. You’ll need to speak confidently about CI/CD, progressive delivery, testing and quality gates, how agent-generated changes affect release risk, and delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. You don’t need to write the code. You do need to know when a customer is describing a real constraint and when they’re describing a habit.

Qualifications:

• Core
• 8+ years of relevant experience, ideally in senior, client-facing roles across product management, delivery, or consulting within B2B SaaS or technology services; or as a forward-deployed/deployment strategist, or early builder/founder at a high-growth tech startup.

• Product and systems thinking: you can define what to deliver and why (MVP or first-phase scoping, prioritization, and success criteria) and manage scope against it.

• Value-based scoping experience (ROI/TCO) with executive buyers, ideally within sales cycles.

• A track record owning both delivery accountability and the executive relationship on the same engagement, with the judgment to decide whether an engagement’s scope still serves the business, not just execute against an agreed plan. Executive-level communication and presence.

• You’ve helped an organization move off an entrenched process and adopt a new way of working, not just documented a better one, including facilitating workshops with mixed engineering and leadership groups and adapting formats on the fly.

• Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, with good judgment about their limits.

• Enough confidence in SDLC and software delivery to be credible with technical stakeholders, and experience partnering closely with technical roles (solutions engineers, architects, or similar).

• Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with progressive delivery and feature management, ideally including LaunchDarkly or a similar tool. Fluency with delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. We’ll teach you the LaunchDarkly specifics.

• Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.

• Experience writing PRDs and managing agile software projects.

• Experience surfacing expansion/renewal signals to Sales or AM; comfort with a role that may take on commercial ownership over time.

• (Bonus) Experience operating in a scaling PS org where role boundaries are still being defined.

Travel

• Travel roughly once per quarter for customer workshops and team onsites; more frequent travel may be needed around specific engagements.

As the Sr. Manager, Critical Situations Team you will lead and manage resolution of our most strategic accounts through challenging periods of their Smartsheet journey. These challenges could be due to user adoption, product issues, solutions scale, professional services, support experience, communication, and/or customer service concerns. This role brings strategy, structure, and executive engagement to marshal company-wide resources to assist customers placed in the Critical Situation (CritSit) process across our global regions. The CritSit process will ensure a high level of customer satisfaction, retention and expansion resulting in both resolution of each customer’s challenges to a healthy state and of continuous improvement and institutional learning from each customer engagement to prevent recurrences across our install base.
You’ll partner closely with GTM leadership of our Customer Success, Professional Services, Support, as well as Sales and Product leadership to build and define the CritSit process methodology and operating model. This role will regularly report out on the status of CritSit customers to our corporate leadership team.
Not only will you be on the front line with many of Smartsheet’s largest customer relationships, but also those struggling with ambitious innovative solution plans intended to lead our install base forward. Your work will be global and highly cross-functional in nature. You will problem-solve alongside leaders in other teams such as Product, Support, Sales, and Finance, to drive resolution and elevate the customer experience.

Role Description
As Director of Pricing and Packaging at Dropbox, you will lead the strategy that determines how we package, price, and monetize our products across product-led growth (PLG) and sales-led growth (SLG) motions. Reporting to Head of Product Marketing, you will lead a small team and partner closely with Product, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Data Science, and senior executives to make pricing and packaging a durable driver of customer value and profitable growth.
This is a highly visible opportunity to help reinvent Dropbox’s monetization approach as we expand our sales-led business and build for the AI era. You will develop a holistic pricing and packaging architecture across products, customer segments, and routes to market—balancing customer adoption, competitive positioning, revenue growth, cost to serve, and margin. You will translate complex analysis into clear strategic choices, build alignment among senior leaders, and establish the capabilities and operating rhythms needed to make consistently strong monetization decisions.
You will have significant exposure to Dropbox’s senior leadership team and the opportunity to shape some of the company’s most consequential growth decisions. Your work will directly influence how customers experience and value Dropbox, how our products go to market, and how the business grows over the long term.

Responsibilities

• Define and lead Dropbox’s company-wide pricing and packaging strategy across PLG and SLG motions, customer segments, product portfolios, and geographies.

• Design the next generation of Dropbox’s packaging and monetization architecture, including approaches for AI-powered products and capabilities, while balancing customer value, adoption, revenue, cost to serve, and margin.

• Build rigorous business cases and financial models to evaluate pricing and packaging opportunities, incorporating demand, willingness to pay, competitive dynamics, usage patterns, unit economics, and potential customer and revenue impacts.

• Partner with Product, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Data Science, and Operations leaders to translate strategy into executable plans, including research, experimentation, rollout, enablement, measurement, and iteration.

• Advise senior executives on high-impact monetization decisions by synthesizing complex quantitative and qualitative evidence into clear recommendations, tradeoffs, and decision frameworks.

• Establish pricing and packaging governance, operating rhythms, performance metrics, and experimentation practices that improve the quality and speed of decision-making across Dropbox.

• Lead, develop, and inspire a small team of pricing and packaging professionals while expanding the organization’s broader monetization capabilities.

Requirements

• 10+ years of experience in pricing, packaging, monetization, growth strategy, strategic finance, product strategy, management consulting, or a related discipline, including substantial experience in B2B SaaS.

• Demonstrated experience developing and implementing pricing or packaging strategies that produced measurable business or customer outcomes.

• Experience with both product-led and sales-led business models, including an understanding of their distinct customer journeys, routes to market, and monetization considerations.

• Experience building pricing business cases and financial models that connect customer behavior and willingness to pay with revenue, cost to serve, unit economics, and margin.

• Working knowledge of SaaS and AI monetization models, including subscription, seat-based, usage-based, consumption-based, and hybrid approaches.

• Demonstrated ability to influence executive-level decisions and align senior cross-functional stakeholders around complex, high-impact initiatives.

• People-management experience, including hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing team members.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading a major pricing or packaging transformation for a multi-product or global SaaS company.

• Experience developing monetization strategies for AI-powered products, including evaluating inference or infrastructure costs, usage economics, value metrics, and margin implications.

• Experience managing the intersection of self-serve, enterprise, and partner-led offerings within a shared product portfolio.

• Experience with pricing research and experimentation methods such as conjoint analysis, willingness-to-pay research, price elasticity analysis, customer segmentation, or controlled testing.

Durable Skills
AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve:

• Awareness: U nderstand yourself and others .

• Judgment: E valuat e information and mak e decisions in complex situations .

• Adaptability: L earn, adjust, and stay effective through change .

• Connection: C ommunicat e , collaborat e , and build trust .

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

jobs.title: Community Engagement Manager, Data Centers (Montana & Utah)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote-Friendly, United States

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.
We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Montana and Utah to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.
You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.
You will travel regularly within Montana and Utah, up to 50% of the time, often over long distances, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets.

Key responsibilities

• Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with county commissioners, mayors and city and town councils, planning and zoning bodies, state economic development agencies (such as Montana's Department of Commerce and Utah's Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity), community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Montana and Utah data center markets you cover

• Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Tribal governments and Native communities in Montana and Utah, recognizing Tribal sovereignty, building sustained relationships, and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects

• Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

• Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

• Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

• Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

• Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced

• Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

• Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

• Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including water availability and water rights in a dry climate and how rural electric cooperatives and utilities would serve large electricity needs

• Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

• Direct experience working for or engaging with county and municipal governments and a broad set of community stakeholders on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out

• A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

• The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

• The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

• Based in Montana or Utah or willing to relocate to one of them, and prepared to travel regularly, including long drives, across both states

Preferred qualifications

• 7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data center, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government

• Familiarity with land use, zoning, and permitting processes at the county and municipal level in Montana and/or Utah, and with water rights and water use questions in the Mountain West

• Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

• Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

• Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

• Experience working with Tribal governments and Native communities in Montana or Utah, including familiarity with consultation processes, Tribal sovereignty and treaty considerations, or community benefit and partnership agreements

• A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$265,000 — $295,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US: Select locations

Role Description
This is a critical leadership role at the intersection of data science, data engineering, finance, and AI. As Director, Data Science & Data Engineering for Finance, you will lead a small, high-impact team that enables Finance to make better decisions through trusted data, robust analytical systems, applied modeling, and increasingly AI-powered capabilities.
You will manage two direct reports: a data scientist and a data engineer. Together, the team supports the financial organization across recurring business operations, driver-model maintenance, knowledge coordination, analytical insights, and the development and operationalization of AI and machine-learning use cases. The role requires enough technical depth to guide both disciplines, while maintaining a clear focus on business outcomes, reliability, and team growth.
You will partner closely with Finance leadership, Engineering, Data, Product, and other cross-functional stakeholders to establish priorities, improve the quality and accessibility of financial data, and shape a forward-looking roadmap. You will be expected to move the team beyond request-driven execution: identifying the highest-leverage opportunities, clarifying the problems worth solving, and creating the operating mechanisms needed to deliver durable impact.
This is an opportunity to shape how Finance uses data and AI at a time when the underlying technologies, operating models, and expectations are changing quickly. The successful candidate will bring a growth mindset, a strong background in either data science or data engineering, and the ability to lead effectively across both disciplines.

Responsibilities

• Manage and grow a multidisciplinary team: Lead, coach, and develop a data scientist and a data engineer, creating clear expectations, meaningful development plans, effective delegation, and a strong culture of ownership and continuous improvement.

• Set the team’s strategy and priorities: Translate Finance and company goals into a focused portfolio of work. Prioritize ruthlessly across strategic initiatives, recurring operational responsibilities, model maintenance, knowledge coordination, and technical debt.

• Provide technical leadership across data science and data engineering: Guide problem framing, analytical and modeling approaches, data architecture, pipeline quality, testing, monitoring, documentation, and production readiness. You do not need to be the deepest expert in both disciplines, but you must be able to ask the right questions, recognize trade-offs, and raise the technical bar.

• Advance AI and modeling capabilities: Identify high-value opportunities to apply AI, machine learning, automation, and advanced analytics to Finance workflows. Establish appropriate standards for experimentation, evaluation, interpretability, human oversight, privacy, and ongoing monitoring.

• Build trusted data foundations: Partner with data engineering and Finance stakeholders to improve source-of-truth datasets, data quality, lineage, observability, documentation, and reliability. Ensure that recurring reporting, driver models, and downstream analyses are based on accurate and well-governed data.

• Own analytical and modeling outcomes: Ensure the team develops, maintains, evaluates, and improves models and analyses that support financial planning, forecasting, business-driver understanding, and decision-making. Connect technical work to measurable business outcomes rather than treating model delivery as the finish line.

• Create scalable operating mechanisms: Establish lightweight processes for intake, prioritization, roadmap planning, model and pipeline reviews, incident response, documentation, knowledge sharing, and stakeholder communication. Reduce dependency on individual heroics and make the team’s work easier to understand and extend.

• Influence Finance and senior stakeholders: Communicate complex data, model, and engineering considerations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Present implications, recommendations, risks, and trade-offs in a way that enables timely decisions.

• Partner across functions: Work effectively with Finance leaders, analysts, data scientists, data engineers, software engineers, product partners, and executives. Seek diverse perspectives, lead productive debate, and align stakeholders when priorities or approaches differ.

• Improve the team’s scope and effectiveness: Look continuously for ways to eliminate low-value work, automate recurring tasks, improve service levels, and increase the team’s strategic contribution. When the current operating model is insufficient, make the case for change and lead the team through it

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree or above in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

• Significant experience applying data science, machine learning, analytics, data engineering, or a combination of these disciplines to business problems.

• Experience directly managing and developing technical professionals, ideally including both data scientists and data engineers or closely adjacent roles.

• A strong professional foundation in either data science or data engineering, with demonstrated ability to work effectively across the other discipline.

• Experience leading a portfolio of projects from problem definition through delivery, adoption, measurement, and ongoing operation.

• Experience with data quality, data pipelines, analytical datasets, model development or maintenance, experimentation or evaluation, and production or operational support.

• Demonstrated ability to use data and technology to influence business decisions and deliver measurable impact.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts, uncertainty, and trade-offs to Finance and executive audiences.

• Demonstrated growth mindset: actively seeks feedback, learns new technologies and domains, adapts to changing conditions, and creates an environment where the team does the same.

• Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting Finance, financial planning and analysis, forecasting, corporate strategy, accounting, or other business functions with high standards for accuracy and control.

• Experience building or scaling AI/ML capabilities, including generative AI, predictive modeling, model evaluation, workflow automation, or AI-assisted decision support.

• Experience managing a hybrid or multidisciplinary team spanning data science, analytics, data engineering, or software engineering.

• Experience building 0-to-1 capabilities, establishing new operating models, or transforming a team from reactive execution to proactive partnership.

• Experience with data governance, observability, model risk management, responsible AI, or other practices that support reliable and auditable business decisions.

• Experience working in a technology company or other complex, data-rich environment.

Durable Skills
AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve:

• Awareness: U nderstand yourself and others .

• Judgment: E valuat e information and mak e decisions in complex situations .

• Connection: C ommunicat e , collaborat e , and build trust .

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

jobs.title: CMC & Manufacturing Lead, Life Sciences
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote-Friendly, United States

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is working to make Claude a useful partner across biology and drug development, so that promising science can reach patients sooner. Genetic medicines are one area where we see real potential, particularly for diseases with few or no treatment options.
Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) often sets the pace in this field. We’re hiring a CMC & Manufacturing Lead to bring deep technical expertise to our team. You’ll guide CMC strategy across a range of genetic medicine technologies, work closely with external partners, and help our researchers and engineers make Claude useful for real CMC work.
Much of today’s CMC practice was built for products made at scale for large populations. You’ll help work out what better approaches could look like for smaller ones, including platform processes, faster testing, and ways to carry knowledge from one product to the next.
If you have deep experience manufacturing genetic medicines and want to explore how AI can help accelerate the way they’re developed, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

• Guide CMC and manufacturing strategy for genetic medicines, from early development through clinical supply

• Serve as a CMC expert to external partners, reviewing process, analytical, and supply plans and resolving technical issues together

• Provide technical oversight of externally conducted process development, formulation, analytical development, fill-finish, stability, and release testing, with phase-appropriate specifications and control strategies

• Collaborate with scientists across disciplines to turn early research into robust, GMP-ready processes

• Oversee quality for externally manufactured material, including audits, quality agreements, and batch disposition

• Evaluate novel manufacturing, analytical, and delivery technologies, and make clear recommendations

• Develop approaches that reduce the time and cost of reaching clinical material without compromising product quality or patient safety

• Work with Anthropic researchers and engineers to identify where Claude can speed up CMC work, contribute to evaluations and tools, and test results against real-world problems

• Identify CMC and supply chain risks early, and communicate status, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly

Minimum qualifications

• Biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience leading CMC for gene therapy, gene editing, or nucleic acid products, including taking a product from preclinical development into the clinic

• Deep expertise in several of the following, and working knowledge of the others: lipid nanoparticles (LNP), mRNA, guide RNA (gRNA), adeno-associated virus (AAV), and antisense oligonucleotides (ASO), including how they are manufactured, characterized, and released

• Deep understanding of GMP manufacturing and regulatory CMC requirements for genetic medicines, including writing or reviewing CMC sections of INDs or equivalent filings

• A strong track record of selecting and managing CDMOs, CROs, and other external partners, including technology transfer and quality oversight

• Demonstrated creativity in manufacturing novel products, shown by process, analytical, or supply solutions you developed where no established precedent existed

• Ability to evaluate novel technologies rigorously from data and turn that evaluation into a clear recommendation

• Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining CMC tradeoffs to people outside the field

• Curiosity about how AI can change drug development, and excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI

Preferred qualifications

• 10+ years in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry, with a focus on CMC and gene therapy product development

• An advanced degree in chemical engineering, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular biology, or a related field

• Experience with rare disease or small-population programs, or with platform-based manufacturing and regulatory approaches

• Direct experience leading CMC discussions with the FDA and other health authorities, such as the EMA and MHRA

• Hands-on experience with GMP quality activities, such as vendor audits, quality agreements, deviation review, and batch disposition

• Experience building a CMC function or working in a fully outsourced model

• Experience with small-batch or rapid-turnaround GMP manufacturing and accelerated release testing

• Experience with technical due diligence on external technologies or manufacturing partners

• Hands-on experience using LLM tools like Claude in your day-to-day work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$300,000 — $320,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, On-Prem
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote) or United States (Remote) or Mexico City, Mexico (Hybrid)

About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the On-Prem Team
The On-Prem team ships CircleCI Server, our self-hosted CI/CD platform for customers who need to run everything inside their own infrastructure: regulated industries, air-gapped environments, and teams with strict data residency and compliance requirements. Our mission is to deliver an on-premises CircleCI that is secure, highly available, and easy to install, upgrade, and support.
Our team serves two kinds of customers: the organizations that run Server, and the CircleCI engineering teams whose services ship inside it. Beyond the product itself, we own the tooling and infrastructure that let those teams package, test, and release their services into Server and keep them current. As a Staff Engineer here, you'll care as much about the internal release experience as about making Server reliable and easy to operate for external customers.

What You'll Do

• Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how we approach and solve problems.

• Make shipping into Server easy for every team. Own the platform strategy, setting the technical direction for the tooling, test infrastructure, and release automation that CircleCI teams use to develop and maintain their services inside Server.

• Give customers confidence installing, upgrading, and running CircleCI Server. Customers run Server in environments you'll never see. Make the install experience simpler and more predictable, upgrades safer, and day-to-day operation easier, starting with sensible defaults.

• Own Server's foundation. You'll be responsible for everything from the Kubernetes infrastructure Server deploys into, to the tooling internal teams and customers depend on. That responsibility extends past your own code to the systems and teams around it.

• Get operators from symptom to root cause fast. Standardize Server's observability on OpenTelemetry so it works with whatever platform each customer already runs. Build diagnostics that help operators, and the engineers supporting them, find the problem quickly. Partner with Support, Customer Engineering, and customers to find recurring issues and fix them at the source.

• Connect engineering to the business. Partner directly with Product and Engineering Management to translate business goals into technical strategy. You understand the "why" behind the roadmap and use it to make tradeoffs.

What You'll Bring

• A platform mindset. You default to building tools, frameworks, and systems that make other engineers more productive rather than solving each problem one-off. You've built internal platforms before and can talk about the leverage they created for the teams that used them.

• AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.

• Deep experience with Kubernetes and Helm. You've designed, deployed, and debugged production systems on Kubernetes. You know where the sharp edges are, especially in customer-operated environments (air-gapped, restricted network, unfamiliar cluster shapes).

• Strong backend and systems foundation. 8+ years building production backend and infrastructure systems, with a history of taking accountability for outcomes. Strong in Go, with real experience in API design, data modelling, distributed systems, and operational tooling.

• System design with business context. You make architecture decisions that span multiple systems and teams, weigh tradeoffs against business needs, and document your reasoning. You're the person others escalate to when the answer isn't obvious.

• Technical leadership. You mentor engineers, give direct feedback on technical direction, and raise the quality bar across teams through how you engage in reviews and design discussions, not just what you ship.

• Experience with on-premises or self-hosted software. You've shipped software that runs in someone else's environment (enterprise on-prem, self-hosted SaaS, or a distributed system installed by customers), and you understand how that constraint shapes your design choices, release process, and support model.

Sound Like You?
You believe the best platform work makes everyone else faster. You're energized by the challenge of building software that has to work in environments you can't see or control.
