job.title: Technical Consultant, ServiceNow - CSM
job.description:
AHEAD builds platforms for digital business. By weaving together advances in cloud infrastructure, automation and analytics, and software delivery, we help enterprises deliver on the promise of digital transformation.
At AHEAD , we prioritize creating a culture of belonging, where all perspectives and voices are represented, valued, respected, and heard. We create spaces to empower everyone to speak up, make change, and drive the culture at AHEAD .
We are an equal opportunity employer, and do not discriminate based on an individual's race, national origin, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law, whether actual or perceived.
We embrace all candidates that will contribute to the diversification and enrichment of ideas and perspectives at AHEAD .
As a Technical Consultant, ServiceNow, you will configure, develop, and implement ServiceNow solutions aligned with business requirements and platform best practices. This role is primarily hands-on and focused on delivery.

You will work closely with Senior Technical Consultants, Principal Consultants, project managers, and client stakeholders to build scalable, supportable, and high-quality solutions. The ideal candidate will have strong experience in one primary ServiceNow product CSM with an exposure to other products such ITSM, ITAM, HRSD, ITOM, or similar modules along with solid platform development skills and a strong focus on code quality, maintainability, and delivery excellence.

Roles & Responsibilities

• Develop, configure, customize, and enhance ServiceNow applications based on business requirements and platform best practices.

• Design and implement solutions in one primary ServiceNow product CSM with an exposure to other products such as ITSM, ITAM, HRSD, ITOM or related modules.

• Build and support workflows, flows, business rules, client scripts, UI policies, portals, workspaces, and integrations as needed.

• Develop and optimize integrations using supported ServiceNow capabilities, APIs, and standard methods.

• Troubleshoot issues, analyze root causes, and implement sustainable fixes.

• Perform unit testing, support QA and UAT, and contribute to code reviews and overall quality.

• Participate in Agile ceremonies, manage assigned priorities, and raise risks or blockers early.

• Maintain technical documentation and stay current with ServiceNow platform capabilities.

Qualifications & Experience

• 3 to 6 years of experience working on the ServiceNow platform in a developer or technical consultant role.

• Strong hands-on experience in one primary ServiceNow product CSM with an exposure to other products such as ITSM, ITAM, HRSD, ITOM or related modules. .

• Solid experience in ServiceNow scripting using JavaScript, Glide APIs, workflows, Flow Designer, and platform customization.

• Good experience with integrations, REST APIs, imports, and automation capabilities within ServiceNow.

• Experience building or supporting Service Portal, Workspace, UI Builder, or related user interface components is preferred.

• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills in a dynamic project environment.

• Good understanding of software development lifecycle principles and structured delivery methods.

• Ability to work independently on assigned tasks while collaborating effectively as part of a project team.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• ServiceNow certifications such as CSA, CAD, or CIS are an advantage, though demonstrated hands-on capability is valued most.

Preferred Attributes

• Strong ownership of assigned work and accountability for delivery of quality.

• Ability to understand business needs and convert them into practical technical solutions.

• Strong attention to documentation, testing, and delivery discipline.

• Willingness to learn new ServiceNow modules and platform capabilities over time.

• Professional, collaborative, and delivery-focused approach.

Success Profile
A successful Technical Consultant in this role will be a strong hands-on builder who can independently deliver assigned technical work, contribute to solution quality, collaborate effectively with the wider delivery team, and bring strong depth in at least one primary ServiceNow product area.

Why AHEAD :
Through our daily work and internal groups like Moving Women AHEAD and RISE AHEAD , we value and benefit from diversity of people, ideas, experience, and everything in between.
We fuel growth by stacking our office with top-notch technologies in a multi-million-dollar lab, by encouraging cross department training and development, sponsoring certifications and credentials for continued learning.

India Employment Benefits include:
Comprehensive health insurance coverage for employees, with options to extend coverage to dependents
Paid time off and company holidays , along with additional leave benefits as per policy
Flexible work arrangements , supporting work-life balance
Learning and development opportunities to support continuous growth and upskilling
Employee wellness initiatives and programs focused on physical and mental well-being
Retirement and statutory benefits in line with India regulations
Inclusive and people-first culture , with a strong focus on collaboration and ownership

Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. Sales, Customer Success, Sales Enablement, Solution Architects, Business Development, Transformation, and Technology Partnerships all work together to demonstrate the power and agility of Zscaler cloud transformation to the world.
About the Role
We are looking for an Account Executive in Civilian to join our Sales and Go-to-Market team focused on SBA, DHA and VA . This role is based in the D.C. area , reporting to the Regional Director. You will be part of a global group of professionals passionate about delighting our customers, nurturing trusted partnerships, and sharing expertise to drive a secure, cloud-enabled digital future. By demonstrating the power and agility of cloud transformation, you will help cement our position as the world leader in cloud security.

• You thrive in ambiguity. You're comfortable building the path as you walk it. You thrive in a dynamic environment, seeing ambiguity not as a hindrance, but as the raw material to build something meaningful.

• You act like an owner. Your passion for the mission fuels your bias for action. You operate with integrity because you genuinely care about the outcome. True ownership involves leveraging dynamic range: the ability to navigate seamlessly between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.

• You are a problem-solver. You love running towards the challenges because you are laser-focused on finding the solution, knowing that solving the hard problems delivers the biggest impact.

• You are a high-trust collaborator. You are ambitious for the team, not just yourself. You embrace our challenge culture by giving and receiving ongoing feedback—knowing that candor delivered with clarity and respect is the truest form of teamwork and the fastest way to earn trust.

• You are a learner. You have a true growth mindset and are obsessed with your own development, actively seeking feedback to become a better partner and a stronger teammate. You love what you do and you do it with purpose.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

• 8+ years of full-cycle sales experience within the software or security industry

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience

• Progressive selling experience engaging with enterprise accounts and selling at the C-Level

• Foundational understanding of AI/ML technologies and experience leveraging, securing, or positioning AI-driven solutions to optimize outcomes within your functional domain

• Established relationships with current and prospective customers and a deep understanding of how technology facilitates high-level business goals

We're hiring a Clearing Risk Analyst to join our Clearing Risk team and help build Coinbase's clearing business, including prediction markets. This team is responsible for how the clearinghouse identifies, measures, and manages risk across clearing-member positions, margin methodologies, and settlement processes.
You'll own defined risk analysis projects from investigation through recommendation, working closely with the DCO risk lead and partnering with Product, Operations, and Finance to turn analysis into practical risk decisions that shape a growing business.

• Analyze clearing-member positions, collateral, settlement obligations, and concentrations, investigating meaningful changes and exceptions and recommending follow-up actions.

• Contribute to margin methodology development and review by analyzing collateral coverage, stress scenarios, and backtesting results, and pressure-testing the assumptions behind them.

• Assess risks arising from new products, business changes, and market events by identifying potential failure scenarios and developing recommendations for the DCO risk lead.

• Build and refine risk reporting and recurring monitoring by validating figures against source records, defining clear metrics, distinguishing missing or stale data from genuine absence of exposure, and simplifying workflows to improve efficiency.

• Partner with Product, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Compliance to evaluate how funding, settlement, and processing failures create financial risk across the trade lifecycle, and help draft and maintain related risk procedures and control documentation.

• Prepare concise risk analyses, incident reviews, and management materials that clearly separate confirmed facts, assumptions, open questions, and recommendations.

• 1 to 3 years of experience in market risk, counterparty risk, derivatives clearing, or trading operations at a major financial institution, exchange, or clearinghouse.

• Working knowledge of derivatives products and margin models, including how trades create positions, funding needs, and settlement obligations, and how initial and variation margin protect against counterparty exposure.

• Familiarity with clearing risk concepts such as stress and backtesting, collateral management, or settlement exception analysis.

• Demonstrated ability to take an open-ended risk question, structure a work plan, source the right data, and deliver a considered recommendation with minimal direction.

• Sound judgment on escalation: You know when an issue requires deeper investigation versus immediate action, and you communicate your limitations clearly.

About the Job:
LaunchDarkly is seeking a Commissions Analyst to help administer accurate, timely commission programs for the Revenue organization. The role will validate commission calculations, maintain commission and quota data in commissions tool, support accrual and payroll submissions, and respond to employee and leader inquiries.
Working with Sales and Customer Success leaders, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Payroll, this analyst will investigate discrepancies, support quota and plan administration, and deliver ad hoc reporting. We’re looking for someone with commission experience, strong spreadsheet skills, curiosity, and attention to detail who will improve how work gets done—automating manual processes and thoughtfully using approved internal AI tools while maintaining appropriate review and controls.

Responsibilities:

• Prepare commission accruals for Finance and commission payment submissions for Payroll according to local Payroll schedules, with accurate supporting analysis and reconciliations

• Support the build and implementation of commission plans in the commission tool; administer employee records and plan inputs

• Calculate individual quota assignments from approved base quotas, partnering with Revenue Operations to validate changes and resolve discrepancies

• Address and resolve any commission or compensation-plan-related inquiries

• Track and administer incentive spiffs, adjustments, and exceptions

• Deliver ad hoc reporting and analysis

• Support compensation plan distribution and track participant review and approval status

• Improve commission processes by standardizing controls, automating repetitive work, and thoughtfully using approved internal AI tools with appropriate human review

• Maintain clear process documentation and audit-ready reconciliations

• Handle confidential compensation data with discretion

Qualifications:

• 3+ years of experience in sales commissions or incentive compensation; experience supporting multiple commissionable roles is preferred

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field preferred, or equivalent experience

• Experience with a commissions platform such as QuotaPath, Xactly, CaptivateIQ, Everstage or similar, and familiarity with Salesforce or related business systems

• Highly proficient Excel and Google Sheets skills, including formulas, lookups, validation workbooks, and reconciling large data sets

• Strong analytical and investigative skills; able to trace discrepancies to source data, understand calculation logic, and explain findings clearly

• Exceptional attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through, with the ability to manage recurring deadlines and competing requests

• Clear written and verbal communication skills and comfort partnering with Sales, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Payroll

job.title: Release Strategist, Professional Services
job.description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

About the Job:
Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.
As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”
Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.
This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

• Product & Value
• Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.

• Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

• Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.

• Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.

• Change & Adoption
• Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.

• Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.

• Executive & Growth
• Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.

• Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.

• Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)
• Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.

• Delivery & Execution
• Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.

• Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.

• Customer Landscape
• Our customers struggle with long lead times, risky deployments, feature flag sprawl, unclear ownership of releases, and a gap between what engineering ships and what the business expects. You’ll need to speak confidently about CI/CD, progressive delivery, testing and quality gates, how agent-generated changes affect release risk, and delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. You don’t need to write the code. You do need to know when a customer is describing a real constraint and when they’re describing a habit.

Qualifications:

• Core
• 8+ years of relevant experience, ideally in senior, client-facing roles across product management, delivery, or consulting within B2B SaaS or technology services; or as a forward-deployed/deployment strategist, or early builder/founder at a high-growth tech startup.

• Product and systems thinking: you can define what to deliver and why (MVP or first-phase scoping, prioritization, and success criteria) and manage scope against it.

• Value-based scoping experience (ROI/TCO) with executive buyers, ideally within sales cycles.

• A track record owning both delivery accountability and the executive relationship on the same engagement, with the judgment to decide whether an engagement’s scope still serves the business, not just execute against an agreed plan. Executive-level communication and presence.

• You’ve helped an organization move off an entrenched process and adopt a new way of working, not just documented a better one, including facilitating workshops with mixed engineering and leadership groups and adapting formats on the fly.

• Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, with good judgment about their limits.

• Enough confidence in SDLC and software delivery to be credible with technical stakeholders, and experience partnering closely with technical roles (solutions engineers, architects, or similar).

• Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with progressive delivery and feature management, ideally including LaunchDarkly or a similar tool. Fluency with delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. We’ll teach you the LaunchDarkly specifics.

• Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.

• Experience writing PRDs and managing agile software projects.

• Experience surfacing expansion/renewal signals to Sales or AM; comfort with a role that may take on commercial ownership over time.

• (Bonus) Experience operating in a scaling PS org where role boundaries are still being defined.

Travel

• Travel roughly once per quarter for customer workshops and team onsites; more frequent travel may be needed around specific engagements.

Pay:
Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level P4:

• Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200 - $235,400 **

• Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860 **

• Zone 3: All other US locations - $145,500 - $200,090* *

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.
*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:
Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations.
The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

• Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

job.description:
Headquarters: -REMOTE, USA-
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smartsheet is a tech company with a human story to tell. We’re here to empower teams to manage projects, automate workflows, and rapidly build new secure solutions, using simple no-code tools. We’re revolutionaries – so for us changing the way the world works is all in a day’s work.
As the Sr. Manager, Critical Situations Team you will lead and manage resolution of our most strategic accounts through challenging periods of their Smartsheet journey. These challenges could be due to user adoption, product issues, solutions scale, professional services, support experience, communication, and/or customer service concerns. This role brings strategy, structure, and executive engagement to marshal company-wide resources to assist customers placed in the Critical Situation (CritSit) process across our global regions. The CritSit process will ensure a high level of customer satisfaction, retention and expansion resulting in both resolution of each customer’s challenges to a healthy state and of continuous improvement and institutional learning from each customer engagement to prevent recurrences across our install base.
You’ll partner closely with GTM leadership of our Customer Success, Professional Services, Support, as well as Sales and Product leadership to build and define the CritSit process methodology and operating model. This role will regularly report out on the status of CritSit customers to our corporate leadership team.
Not only will you be on the front line with many of Smartsheet’s largest customer relationships, but also those struggling with ambitious innovative solution plans intended to lead our install base forward. Your work will be global and highly cross-functional in nature. You will problem-solve alongside leaders in other teams such as Product, Support, Sales, and Finance, to drive resolution and elevate the customer experience.
You will report to the VP of Customer Experience, Programs and Strategy. This is a remote eligible position and you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is registered.
You Will:

• Lead executive meetings and strategic content with respect and visibility among executives.

• Leads cross-functional, business-wide efforts through effective thought leadership.

• Analyzes resolution path for high-stakes issues, and develops a strategy and gain alignment across executives for an effective and efficient solution.

• Ensures outcomes that affect the entire product, company, and/or customer base.

• Key point of contact for resolving critical issues.

• Provide quantitative results on the effectiveness and value of the team tied to business impact and strategy.

• Expanded scope of leadership within the broader department, outside of just the CritSit team.

• Develop and own our Critical Situation methodology, response playbook and processes, including any regional variants

• Develop nomination, entry and exit criteria for accounts such that Critical SItuation is a time bound need, restoring confidence and success within accounts to be promoted out of the program

• Identify process gaps and themes with product and engineering to drive change and ensure timely customer communication

• Determine the methods to incorporate our technology landscape (Salesforce Sales, Salesforce Service, Smartsheet, Gainsight, Seismic, Chorus, ZoomInfo, Jira, etc.)

• Develop systems and tools for visibility and coordination with internal teams and the customer

• Persuade, influence, and motivate people; build a culture of creating delightful customer experiences and relationships

• Engage with and lead cross-functional communications while accounts are in Critical Situation to ensure internal and external customers are receiving status updates

• Lead Executive communications with customers as necessary during Critical Situation

• Influence roadmap prioritization with Product and Engineering to resolve customer challenges

• Have the flexibility in your working hours to team with global customers, and willingness to be “on call” for your CritSit accounts

• Participate in leadership and customer meetings

You Have:

• 5+ years of experience managing globally diverse, large, and cross-functional initiatives

• 3+ years of experience using the Smartsheet Platform

• Implemented SaaS technology in large enterprise settings as a leader of customer or services teams

• Understanding of SaaS organizational and operational constructs including Product, engineering, support, success, sales, services

• Ability to quickly establish trust and to influence others, both internally and externally

• Ability to handle conflict and drive agreement on decisions for which conflicting opinions and input exist

• Strong data-driven decision making skills, and process oriented mindset

• Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement approaches

• Ability to identify risks and dependencies and put in place plans to mitigate them

• Adaptability, flexibility and the conviction to “do the right thing” by keeping a customer centric mentality at all times

• Ability to deal with ambiguity, utilize robust problem solving skills, demonstrate situational agility, manage parallel efforts, and communicate effectively through multiple channels

• Exceptional business acumen and world-class presentation and customer interaction skills that have been acquired through deep technical knowledge and well-developed process management

• Goal orientation to drive progress for each customer through each interaction

• Experience building, leading or teaming with teams similar to HyperCare at a mature technology company, optional but highly desired

• Experience with Smartsheet, Kibana, Snowflake, Tableau, Sparkpost, and Google Suite optional but highly desired

• Knowledge of the Smartsheet platform optional but highly desired

job.title: Community Engagement Manager, Data Centers (Montana & Utah)
job.description:
Headquarters: Remote-Friendly, United States

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.
We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Montana and Utah to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.
You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.
You will travel regularly within Montana and Utah, up to 50% of the time, often over long distances, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets.

Key responsibilities

• Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with county commissioners, mayors and city and town councils, planning and zoning bodies, state economic development agencies (such as Montana's Department of Commerce and Utah's Governor's Office of Economic Opportunity), community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Montana and Utah data center markets you cover

• Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Tribal governments and Native communities in Montana and Utah, recognizing Tribal sovereignty, building sustained relationships, and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects

• Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

• Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

• Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

• Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

• Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced

• Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

• Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

• Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including water availability and water rights in a dry climate and how rural electric cooperatives and utilities would serve large electricity needs

• Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

• Direct experience working for or engaging with county and municipal governments and a broad set of community stakeholders on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out

• A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

• The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

• The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

• Based in Montana or Utah or willing to relocate to one of them, and prepared to travel regularly, including long drives, across both states

Preferred qualifications

• 7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data center, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government

• Familiarity with land use, zoning, and permitting processes at the county and municipal level in Montana and/or Utah, and with water rights and water use questions in the Mountain West

• Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

• Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

• Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

• Experience working with Tribal governments and Native communities in Montana or Utah, including familiarity with consultation processes, Tribal sovereignty and treaty considerations, or community benefit and partnership agreements

• A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$265,000 — $295,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role
Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is working to make Claude a useful partner across biology and drug development, so that promising science can reach patients sooner. Genetic medicines are one area where we see real potential, particularly for diseases with few or no treatment options.

You’ll guide CMC strategy across a range of genetic medicine technologies, work closely with external partners, and help our researchers and engineers make Claude useful for real CMC work.
Much of today’s CMC practice was built for products made at scale for large populations. You’ll help work out what better approaches could look like for smaller ones, including platform processes, faster testing, and ways to carry knowledge from one product to the next.
If you have deep experience manufacturing genetic medicines and want to explore how AI can help accelerate the way they’re developed, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

• Guide CMC and manufacturing strategy for genetic medicines, from early development through clinical supply

• Serve as a CMC expert to external partners, reviewing process, analytical, and supply plans and resolving technical issues together

• Provide technical oversight of externally conducted process development, formulation, analytical development, fill-finish, stability, and release testing, with phase-appropriate specifications and control strategies

• Collaborate with scientists across disciplines to turn early research into robust, GMP-ready processes

• Oversee quality for externally manufactured material, including audits, quality agreements, and batch disposition

• Evaluate novel manufacturing, analytical, and delivery technologies, and make clear recommendations

• Develop approaches that reduce the time and cost of reaching clinical material without compromising product quality or patient safety

• Work with Anthropic researchers and engineers to identify where Claude can speed up CMC work, contribute to evaluations and tools, and test results against real-world problems

• Identify CMC and supply chain risks early, and communicate status, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly

Minimum qualifications

• Biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience leading CMC for gene therapy, gene editing, or nucleic acid products, including taking a product from preclinical development into the clinic

• Deep expertise in several of the following, and working knowledge of the others: lipid nanoparticles (LNP), mRNA, guide RNA (gRNA), adeno-associated virus (AAV), and antisense oligonucleotides (ASO), including how they are manufactured, characterized, and released

• Deep understanding of GMP manufacturing and regulatory CMC requirements for genetic medicines, including writing or reviewing CMC sections of INDs or equivalent filings

• A strong track record of selecting and managing CDMOs, CROs, and other external partners, including technology transfer and quality oversight

• Demonstrated creativity in manufacturing novel products, shown by process, analytical, or supply solutions you developed where no established precedent existed

• Ability to evaluate novel technologies rigorously from data and turn that evaluation into a clear recommendation

• Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining CMC tradeoffs to people outside the field

• Curiosity about how AI can change drug development, and excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI

Preferred qualifications

• 10+ years in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry, with a focus on CMC and gene therapy product development

• An advanced degree in chemical engineering, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular biology, or a related field

• Experience with rare disease or small-population programs, or with platform-based manufacturing and regulatory approaches

• Direct experience leading CMC discussions with the FDA and other health authorities, such as the EMA and MHRA

• Hands-on experience with GMP quality activities, such as vendor audits, quality agreements, deviation review, and batch disposition

• Experience building a CMC function or working in a fully outsourced model

• Experience with small-batch or rapid-turnaround GMP manufacturing and accelerated release testing

• Experience with technical due diligence on external technologies or manufacturing partners

• Hands-on experience using LLM tools like Claude in your day-to-day work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.
For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$300,000 — $320,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

job.description:
Headquarters: Remote, Poland
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
* Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role
As a Backend Engineer on the Plan: Spec-Driven Development team, you'll help build GitLab's intent-to-code loop: agentic workflows that turn a stated intent into a refined work item, an implementation plan, and verified, mergeable code. You'll own early-stage backend work across the flows, application programming interfaces, data models, and evaluation systems behind this experience, using Ruby on Rails, Python, PostgreSQL, GitLab Duo Agent Platform, large language model application programming interfaces, and an artificial intelligence gateway.
You'll join a small, distributed team working on one of GitLab's highest-visibility product bets, collaborating with design partners toward a public beta. In your first year, you'll lead major features from an unclear problem through release, help shape scope with product and users, mentor other engineers, and influence technical decisions across agent workflows and evaluation methods.

What you’ll do

• Lead backend features from early product discussions through technical design, implementation, rollout, and post-launch learning.

• Build the flows, application programming interfaces, and data models behind agent-generated work items, implementation plans, durable specifications, and mergeable code.

• Develop evaluation and benchmarking systems that measure workflow quality, token cost, and success rate.

• Use Ruby on Rails and Python to build reliable production systems, with PostgreSQL, GraphQL, representational state transfer, GitLab Duo Agent Platform, large language model application programming interfaces, and an artificial intelligence gateway.

• Collaborate directly with product, design, engineers, design partners, and users to shape scope and make practical trade-offs.

• Coordinate multi-person projects across the team and communicate decisions clearly in GitLab's asynchronous, all-remote environment.

• Mentor other engineers and contribute to technical direction across the Plan group and related artificial intelligence initiatives.

• Work in short iterations, share progress through demos, and use results and user feedback to guide what comes next.

• Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you’ll bring

• Strong Ruby on Rails experience in a large production codebase and production experience with Python.

• Experience driving substantial projects with several engineers over multiple months, with clear user or business outcomes.

• A product mindset and experience owning features end to end, including shaping scope, making trade-offs, engaging with users, and learning from adoption after launch.

• A full stack background with a current focus on backend engineering, plus the ability to read modern frontend code and design effective APIs.

• Strong application programming interface design and structured query language fundamentals.

• Experience exploring artificial intelligence-assisted development.

• The ability to work independently, collaborate across functions and regions, and support others through technical leadership and mentoring. Experience with GraphQL, PostgreSQL performance at scale, or building and evaluating large language model or agent systems is helpful but not required.

We welcome candidates with different backgrounds and transferable experience. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply.

About the team
We are a team of four engineers, with two backend and two frontend engineers across Canada and Europe. You'll work in an all-remote, async-first environment with weekly sync calls, retrospectives, demos, and short iterations. This is early-stage work with broad ownership, space for creativity, and a fast pace. For more about our team and its work, see Plan Team Handbook Page and Spec-Driven Development Initiative

job.title: Staff Software Engineer, On-Prem
job.description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote) or United States (Remote) or Mexico City, Mexico (Hybrid)

About CircleCI Engineering
CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.
At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the On-Prem Team
The On-Prem team ships CircleCI Server, our self-hosted CI/CD platform for customers who need to run everything inside their own infrastructure: regulated industries, air-gapped environments, and teams with strict data residency and compliance requirements. Our mission is to deliver an on-premises CircleCI that is secure, highly available, and easy to install, upgrade, and support.
Our team serves two kinds of customers: the organizations that run Server, and the CircleCI engineering teams whose services ship inside it. Beyond the product itself, we own the tooling and infrastructure that let those teams package, test, and release their services into Server and keep them current. As a Staff Engineer here, you'll care as much about the internal release experience as about making Server reliable and easy to operate for external customers.

What You'll Do

• Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how we approach and solve problems.

• Make shipping into Server easy for every team. Own the platform strategy, setting the technical direction for the tooling, test infrastructure, and release automation that CircleCI teams use to develop and maintain their services inside Server.

• Give customers confidence installing, upgrading, and running CircleCI Server. Customers run Server in environments you'll never see. Make the install experience simpler and more predictable, upgrades safer, and day-to-day operation easier, starting with sensible defaults.

• Own Server's foundation. You'll be responsible for everything from the Kubernetes infrastructure Server deploys into, to the tooling internal teams and customers depend on. That responsibility extends past your own code to the systems and teams around it.

• Get operators from symptom to root cause fast. Standardize Server's observability on OpenTelemetry so it works with whatever platform each customer already runs. Build diagnostics that help operators, and the engineers supporting them, find the problem quickly. Partner with Support, Customer Engineering, and customers to find recurring issues and fix them at the source.

• Connect engineering to the business. Partner directly with Product and Engineering Management to translate business goals into technical strategy. You understand the "why" behind the roadmap and use it to make tradeoffs.

What You'll Bring

• A platform mindset. You default to building tools, frameworks, and systems that make other engineers more productive rather than solving each problem one-off. You've built internal platforms before and can talk about the leverage they created for the teams that used them.

• AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.

• Deep experience with Kubernetes and Helm. You've designed, deployed, and debugged production systems on Kubernetes. You know where the sharp edges are, especially in customer-operated environments (air-gapped, restricted network, unfamiliar cluster shapes).

• Strong backend and systems foundation. 8+ years building production backend and infrastructure systems, with a history of taking accountability for outcomes. Strong in Go, with real experience in API design, data modelling, distributed systems, and operational tooling.

• System design with business context. You make architecture decisions that span multiple systems and teams, weigh tradeoffs against business needs, and document your reasoning. You're the person others escalate to when the answer isn't obvious.

• Technical leadership. You mentor engineers, give direct feedback on technical direction, and raise the quality bar across teams through how you engage in reviews and design discussions, not just what you ship.

• Experience with on-premises or self-hosted software. You've shipped software that runs in someone else's environment (enterprise on-prem, self-hosted SaaS, or a distributed system installed by customers), and you understand how that constraint shapes your design choices, release process, and support model.

Sound Like You?
You believe the best platform work makes everyone else faster. You're energized by the challenge of building software that has to work in environments you can't see or control. You want to take a product customers depend on and make it dramatically easier to build, ship, and run, both for them and for the teams whose services live inside it. If that sounds like you, let's talk.

How CircleCI Uses AI in Hiring
At CircleCI, people make our hiring decisions. We use technology to support our recruiting team so they can spend more time on what matters most: getting to know you.
Where we may use AI

• Job descriptions and messaging : AI may help draft job descriptions and role-specific messaging so they are clear and accurate.

• Application review : For some roles, we use an AI tool to review applications, including resumes and application responses, against criteria our hiring team sets for the role. The tool generates a fit score and summary to help recruiters organize and prioritize applications.

• Interview notes : With advance notice, an AI note-taking tool may join interviews to record, transcribe, and summarize the conversation. This lets interviewers focus on talking with you. You will be told before each interview, and you may opt out at any stage by letting your recruiter know. If you opt out, the tool will not join, and your candidacy is not affected.

• Outreach : AI may help draft candidate outreach and scheduling messages, which our team reviews before sending.

Our commitment
AI does not make hiring decisions at CircleCI. Our recruiters and hiring teams review candidates and make every decision to advance or reject an application. No candidate is rejected based solely on an AI score. We have tools and processes in place to test for bias and to review how these tools perform, and we adjust our approach as AI technology and the laws that govern it change.
Your choices
You can ask for human-only review of your application, opt out of AI interview note-taking, request an accommodation, or ask questions about how we use AI. Contact recruiting@circleci.com . For how we handle your data, including retention, see our Privacy Policy.

job.description:
Headquarters: Remote, US
At JFrog, we’re reinventing DevOps to help the world’s greatest companies innovate -- and we want you along for the ride. This is a special place with a unique combination of brilliance, spirit and just all-around great people. Here, if you’re willing to do more, your career can take off. And since software plays a central role in everyone’s lives, you’ll be part of an important mission. Thousands of customers, including the majority of the Fortune 100, trust JFrog to manage, accelerate, and secure their software delivery from code to production -- a concept we call “liquid software.” Wouldn't it be amazing if you could join us in our journey?
We are looking for a Senior Technical Project Manager who will manage high-complexity projects to successful completion from initiation through delivery to closure. In this role, you will coordinate with cross-functional teams and our global customers to complete distinct projects both on time and within budget. You will be responsible for driving customer engagement operations that raise the bar for how JFrog Professional Services consultants interact with customers, resources, systems, and data to optimize engagement delivery. Project Managers need to have substantial experience managing software projects and relying on traditional systems and software development methodologies, as well as practical experience with agile project management methodologies.
The ideal candidate will possess a mix of technical consulting, and software development or DevOps project management experience . In this role, you will work cross-functionally, own several small, medium and large projects, and be committed to driving outcomes for customers by following JFrog delivery best practices and continuously improve the process.

As a Senior Technical Project Manager in JFrog you will...

• Develop and manage projects from ideation through execution, including project scope, timeline, and project execution, and coordinate closely with engineers and Architects.

• Proactively develop and manage a backlog of user stories or activities to drive a project forward.

• Address bottlenecks, provide escalation management, anticipate and make tradeoffs and balance the business needs versus technical constraints.

• Provide consistent, executive-level reporting on project status and outcomes to customers and internal stakeholders.

• Demonstrate effective communication skills (both verbal and written) across all levels of the business.

• Contribute to the long-term direction for optimizing project delivery in professional services.

To be a Senior Technical Project Manager in JFrog you need...

• Knowledge of specific industry project management and technical delivery methodologies for software (e.g., Project Management Institute (PMI) methodologies, agile/scrum, and/or software SDLC).

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science or related field.

• Demonstrated progressive experience working as a project manager on Software Delivery or complex technical projects with enterprise customers.

• Experience using various project management and/or agile tools.

• Demonstrate strong communication skills across all levels of the business from technical partners to senior leadership.

• Demonstrated experience with structured thinking to proactively recognize business challenges, map business processes, gather business requirements, evaluate tools, develop roadmaps, devise/recommend solutions, and communicate complex ideas.

• Self-starter attitude with the ability to work with very little guidance and direction.

• Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining strict attention to detail.

• Understanding of software development lifecycle, preferably experience in an agile and/or DevOps environment.

• Demonstrated ability to think strategically about business, products, and technical challenges.

WHAT JFROG CAN OFFER…

job.description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase .

The CTO organization spans 700+ people across Platform, AI, Engineering, Enterprise Engineering and IT. The Chief of Staff to the CTO is a one-person force multiplier. You own the CTO's time, attention, decisions, and follow-through, and increasingly you build the AI agents that run their operating system.

What you'll do

• Own the CTO's operating system: how their week, preparation, and decisions flow, with a running decision and commitment log so decisions get made once, stick, and each follow-up has a named owner.

• Be where they cannot be: represent them in forums and cross-functional discussions across Platform, AI, Engineering, Core, and the executive team, bring back the signal, and unblock without escalation.

• Carry their voice: write and edit town halls, AMAs, all-hands remarks, board materials, and Slack posts so their point of view lands crisply and on time.

• Build and scale AI agents that absorb more of their operating system, freeing your hours for higher-leverage work.

• Run the few things they own that have no organizational home, from framing to clean handoff, without adding process.

Required skills and experience

• 6+ years in BizOps, strategy, consulting, or technical program leadership, including support of a senior technical executive.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication: you can write in an executive's voice and turn technical trade-offs into business terms.

• Technical fluency: you follow architecture, infrastructure, and AI discussions with staff-plus engineers and ask the right questions. You do not need to be a practicing engineer.

• Judgment and discretion with sensitive org, people, and strategy information, and a clear read on what to escalate, decide, or let go.

• Influence without authority across senior engineering and cross-functional leaders, earned by being prepared and useful.

• Personal operating rigor: you track commitments and close loops relentlessly, without building process.

• Hands-on use of AI tools in your own work; experience in a platform, infrastructure, developer tooling, or AI-focused organization is a plus.

• Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

• Experience with programming languages like Golang, Java, C, or Node.js.

• Knowledge of Object-Oriented design and Microservice Architecture.

• Experience with scalable, high-availability applications.

• Comfort working in Linux command line environments.

• A degree in Computer Science or equivalent industry experience.

• Legally eligible to work in Bulgaria on an ongoing basis.

• Fluency in English is required.

Nice to Have:

• Experience with DynamoDB, MySQL, or other relational and non-relational databases.

At Smartsheet, your ideas are heard, your potential is supported, and your contributions have real impact. You’ll have the freedom to explore, push boundaries, and grow beyond your role. job.description:
Headquarters: Remote, United Kingdom
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers how agents are created, shared and connected to tools inside and outside GitLab, how they run, and how their work shows up and can be observed across GitLab.
In this role you'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.

What you'll do

• Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the GitLab monolith (Ruby) and, where needed, the AI Gateway (Python). Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.

• Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.

• Design, implement and review GraphQL and REST APIs and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients.

• Improve and extend automated testing (RSpec and other frameworks) to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.

• Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.

• Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.

• Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class.

What you'll bring

• Experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, including background jobs, APIs and data models.

• Comfort working across the stack in a mature codebase. Familiarity with Python backends and/or Vue frontends is a plus.

• Skill in designing or extending REST and/or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.

• Real enthusiasm for AI and hands-on experience using AI tools in your daily work. Experience designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or integrations is a plus.

• Proven SQL and experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including writing efficient queries and data modeling.

• Experience finding and fixing performance bottlenecks in applications.

• Clear written and verbal communication, including technical proposals and documentation, in a remote, async, cross-functional team.

• Openness to learning and to applying skills from related technologies or fields.

About the team
The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. We provide the platform, catalog and execution features that help teams deliver resilient agents and flows to customers. The stage has three groups: Agent Developer, AI Catalog and Agent Execution, they provide the core harness for GitLab’s agents, the tools Agent’s need to interact with GitLab as well as ways to configure and execute Agents across GitLab.

Our engineers work async-first across EMEA and AMER timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.
